purpose: Maps each of the app's 10 destination-country options to the competitive/entrance exams relevant to studying there, so the 'Are you preparing for any competitive exam?' question can show only exams relevant to the country/countries the visitor already picked in the destinations step, instead of one long undifferentiated list.
country_list_note: This is the same 10-option destination list already used in the app (9 named countries + Other), matching the stakeholder's 'top 10 countries' request.

exams.name: JEE Main
exams.for: Engineering (NITs, most engineering colleges)

exams.name: JEE Advanced
exams.for: Engineering (IITs) — requires qualifying JEE Main first

exams.name: NEET-UG
exams.for: Medicine, dentistry, AYUSH courses

exams.name: CLAT
exams.for: Law (National Law Universities)

exams.name: CUET (UG)
exams.for: Central universities and many state/private universities, all streams

exams.name: State CET (e.g. KCET, MHT-CET, WBJEE, COMEDK)
exams.for: State engineering/professional colleges — ask which state

exams.name: BITSAT
exams.for: BITS Pilani campuses

exams.name: VITEEE
exams.for: VIT campuses

India.note: This is Pedagogy's core counselling territory (NEET/JEE/CET already named in the business context) — this list should be treated as the most important one to get right and to keep current each cycle.

exams.name: EmSAT
exams.for: Mandatory placement/admission test (Math, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Arabic, English) for UAE federal universities (e.g. UAEU, HCT) and many private universities — required regardless of A-Level/IB/CBSE results

exams.name: SAT
exams.for: Optional but strengthens applications and scholarship eligibility, especially for American-curriculum-track private universities

United Arab Emirates.note: English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) is commonly also requested but is a language test, not a competitive/subject exam — keep it out of this list unless the app later adds a separate language-requirements question.

exams.name: UCAT
exams.for: Medicine and dentistry (BMAT was discontinued after the 2024 admissions cycle — UCAT is now the standard test)

exams.name: LNAT
exams.for: Law at several top law schools

exams.name: TMUA
exams.for: Mathematics and some Computer Science courses at a number of universities

exams.name: ESAT
exams.for: Engineering/Natural Sciences/Computer Science at a small group of universities (e.g. Cambridge, Imperial) — replaced the older ENGAA/NSAA tests from 2024 entry

United Kingdom.note: Most UK applicants don't sit any admissions test at all — these apply only to specific competitive courses/universities. Verify against the specific university before finalizing question copy.

exams.name: TestAS
exams.for: Mandatory for non-EU/EEA applicants to bachelor's degrees at many German public universities; optional but useful as a tiebreaker for EU applicants to competitive Numerus-Clausus programs (medicine, dentistry, psychology, top Computer Science)

exams.name: APS Certificate
exams.for: Not an exam — a mandatory academic-credentials verification process/interview required for Indian (and Chinese, Vietnamese) students before a German student visa can be issued. Commonly asked about in the same breath as TestAS, so keep it listed here even though it isn't a test to 'prepare for' in the usual sense.

exams.name: TestDaF / DSH
exams.for: German-language proficiency — only relevant if the chosen program is taught in German rather than English

exams.name: SAT
exams.for: Used by NUS, NTU and SMU to evaluate applicants presenting non-Singaporean qualifications (e.g. Indian CBSE/ISC/CISCE boards) — the standard extra requirement for Indian applicants

Singapore.note: There is no separate Singapore-national entrance exam for foreign applicants — admission is mainly on board results (A-Level/IB/CBSE/etc.) plus SAT.

exams.name: HPAT-Ireland
exams.for: Medicine and some health-profession programmes at 6 Irish universities (Trinity, UCD, UCC, Galway, Limerick, RCSI) — note: international/non-EU applicants are often exempt depending on the university and programme, so this needs a follow-up question or counsellor check rather than being assumed

Ireland.note: CAO (the points-based admissions system) applies to Irish/EU Leaving Certificate students, not to international applicants presenting other qualifications, so it isn't listed here as an 'exam.'

exams.name: SAT / ACT
exams.for: Optional at most Canadian universities but strengthens applications and scholarship chances

exams.name: MCAT
exams.for: Medicine (graduate-entry)

exams.name: LSAT
exams.for: Law

exams.name: GRE / GMAT
exams.for: Graduate programmes and MBA

Canada.note: English-proficiency tests (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/CELPIP/CAEL) are also commonly required but are language tests, not competitive/subject exams — kept out of this list for the same reason as UAE.

exams.name: UCAT ANZ
exams.for: Medicine and dentistry — mandatory for most direct-entry undergraduate medical programmes

exams.name: ISAT
exams.for: An alternate pathway test used by some medicine/health-science programmes

exams.name: GAMSAT
exams.for: Graduate-entry medicine and veterinary science

exams.name: SAT / ACT
exams.for: Optional for general undergraduate admission

exams.name: GRE / GMAT
exams.for: Graduate programmes and MBA

exams.name: SAT / ACT
exams.for: Undergraduate admission (many US universities are now test-optional — still worth asking, since a strong score still helps scholarships)

exams.name: GRE
exams.for: Most graduate (Master's/PhD) programmes

exams.name: GMAT
exams.for: MBA and business Master's programmes

exams.name: MCAT
exams.for: Medical school

exams.name: LSAT
exams.for: Law school

Other.note: No fixed list — when 'Other' is the only or an additional destination, show a free-text 'Which exam(s)?' field instead of a chip list, and flag the record for a counsellor to follow up rather than guessing at a country-specific list.

app_integration_notes: New question, gated by a simple Yes/No: 'Are you preparing for any competitive exam?' Show it after the destination-country selection (Path Swipe deck / grid step) is answered, since it depends on that answer.

If Yes: build the exam chip list dynamically from this file, keyed off whichever countries the visitor selected in the destinations step. If they selected more than one country, union the exam lists (dedupe exact name matches like 'SAT / ACT' or 'GRE / GMAT' that appear under multiple countries) and group them under their country/subheading so it's clear which exam applies where, rather than one flattened list.
If No: skip straight past this question, same as any other optional preference step — don't force an answer.
If 'Other' is the only destination chosen (or included alongside named countries with no exam data), fall back to a free-text field per the 'Other' entry's note above.

This reuses the same interaction pattern as the destinations step itself (tap chips, not swipe) — see the structural-reference note in CLAUDE.md / session_handoff.md about using reference/pedagogy-expo.html's chip-based preferences(2) step (which already had a flat, non-country-aware 'exams' chip list) as the starting point, now made country-aware using this file.
